audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty prose treats Neeko as a generic skillshot mage and never explains what makes the lane hard, and every reference uses male pronouns.
audit.why: Annie is 53.5% over 428 games. The difficulty is entirely Tangle-Barbs (E, 1000 range, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s): Annie has no dash, so a root is a free full combo.
audit.corrected: Slightly favoured for Annie, decided by whether you step forward on Tangle-Barbs' cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[].side read Skill while win[3..6] read Annie, so the page answers 'who wins level 4-5' two different ways.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Skill, Skill, Skill, Annie, Annie, Annie, Annie] and the content layer already matches it.
audit.corrected: Flip phases[3..6].side to Annie as one group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Pop Blossom is called an 'AoE root ultimate' in whys[4], mid and spikes[1]; wants.you[0] calls the root her Q; the cooldown advice says to dodge Tangle-Barbs 'behind minions'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Pop Blossom knocks up nearby enemies then stuns on landing — it is a knock-up plus stun, not a root. The root is Tangle-Barbs (E); Blooming Burst (Q) is the seed. And Tangle-Barbs becomes larger, faster and roots longer if it kills a unit or passes through a champion, so hiding behind a low-health minion makes the root worse, not safer.
audit.corrected: Name Tangle-Barbs as the root, dodge it in open ground rather than behind killable minions, and treat Pop Blossom as a visible wind-up you can stun — except while she is disguised, when the preparation is hidden.

audit.whatIsWrong: Inherent Glamour is mentioned only as a vague 'disguise trick'; the fact that it hides Pop Blossom's preparation is absent.
audit.why: Riot's R text states the preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised — that is the one thing that kills an Annie who is holding her stun for the wind-up.
audit.corrected: Treat any ally-looking champion walking at you as a possible Pop Blossom and pre-stun rather than react.

edits.before: Carry through the one button — Flash-Tibbers on two is a won fight; your whole game is engineering the radius.
edits.after: Carry through the one button — Neeko has no dash out of Tibbers, so a landed stun on her is a dead Neeko.

edits.before: If Neeko takes first blood, tighten up: Tangle-Barbs (Root) is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q refunds and stay relevant through stocked-stun threat.
edits.after: If Neeko takes first blood, tighten up: assume Tangle-Barbs is always up. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn't — farm with Q refunds and step forward only with the stocked stun.

edits.after: At four stacks: walk forward, Q-stun, W, auto, walk away re-stacking off the wave — a guaranteed chunk she cannot root out of.

edits.before: Spending the stocked stun on wave-clear with his engage loaded — unstacked Annie is the most killable mage in the lane.
edits.after: Spending the stocked stun on wave-clear with Tangle-Barbs up — unstacked Annie is the most killable mage in the lane.

edits.before: The root sets up her whole burst — sidestep it behind minions. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Tangle-Barbs roots longer once it passes a champion — never eat it second. Unspent, every step forward is a coin flip.

edits.after: Molten Shield burns whoever strikes you, so pop it as Tangle-Barbs flies — the root lands on a shielded Annie who still stuns.

edits.after: Pop Blossom knocks up then stuns after a wind-up you can see — stun her out of the preparation and Tibbers wins the race.

edits.before: Annie's Tibbers-backed all-in edges out Neeko's AoE root ultimate in a straight damage race at level 6.
edits.after: Annie's Tibbers all-in beats Pop Blossom's knock-up-then-stun wind-up in a straight damage race at 6.

edits.before: This stays a mutual read through level 5: Neeko's root sets up heavy burst damage just like your stun does, so cooldown tracking and positioning decide most trades rather than raw stats. Level 6 brings her AoE root ultimate online which is genuinely scary in skirmishes, but your own Tibbers-backed all-in combo now edges out her damage in a straight burst race, especially if you force the fight before she's fully set up.
edits.after: This stays a mutual read through level 5: Tangle-Barbs sets up heavy burst just like your stun does, and it roots for longer if it clips a champion first, so cooldown tracking and spacing decide most trades rather than raw stats. Level 6 brings Pop Blossom online — a knock-up into a stun after a short wind-up — but your Tibbers-backed all-in edges out her damage in a burst race, especially if you stun her during the preparation.

edits.before: Bait her Q root with minion positioning before committing your combo
edits.after: Bait Tangle-Barbs in open ground before committing your stun combo

edits.before: Land her root first to lock down your all-in potential
edits.after: Land Tangle-Barbs through a minion so the root lasts longer

edits.before: Use disguise to set up surprise engages or escapes
edits.after: Use Inherent Glamour to hide the Pop Blossom wind-up

notes: Three separate places called Pop Blossom a root ultimate; it is a knock-up followed by a stun. wants.you[0] attributed the root to Neeko's Q — the root is Tangle-Barbs (E), the Q is Blooming Burst. The old cooldown advice ('sidestep it behind minions') was actively harmful: Tangle-Barbs grows larger, faster and roots longer after killing a unit. Level chart: full layer read Skill on all seven rows while content and packet both give Annie rows 3-6; flipped as one atomic group. Neeko is female and the shared boilerplate in phases[0-3].why and several report entries still says 'he' — left alone to avoid conflicting with champion-level template edits.
